newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish shares close lower on fears rally now behind.
newsitem.headline: Finnish shares close lower on fears rally now behind.

text.p: Finnish shares ended lower almost across the board on Tuesday, still smarting from a central bank warning on asset values on Monday, which sparked fears that stocks may be in for a fall after a recent record-breaking streak, brokers said.
The FOX stock futures index ended 1.08 percent lower at 1,066.60, while the all-share HEX closed off 0.83 percent at 3,111.43 points -- both indices still up some 24 percent this year.
Volume was a moderately active 430 million markka with telecoms blue-chip Nokia accounting for 40 percent.
Nokia fell 5.9 markka or 1.6 percent to 359.00 markka, hurt by its lower overnight close in New York as well as by a weaker start on Wall Street on Tuesday, brokers said.
In connection with a warning that increased inflation risks may call for tighter monetary policy, Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen on Monday also said asset values had been rising sharply.
"The governor's talk that what goes up must come down really awoke fears that the stock market rally may be coming to an end," one broker said.
Neste bucked Tuesday's trend, closing 0.50 markka higher at 138.50 on prospects of a merger with state-owned power company IVO. It briefly touched a 15-week high at 145.00 markka.
